editorial_rationale: Described as electronic pop throughout; hooks remain pop-centred.
Described as electronic pop (canonical electropop descriptor).
Cavernous electronics and programmed electronic production are an album signature.
Bridges PC Music styles and radio-oriented dance-pop; club-oriented tracks recur.
Later signed NME retrospective explicitly mentions trap beats throughout the tape.
Apple Music cites the Auto-Tuned hip-hop sound on Dreamer.
Pitchfork groups this release under pop/R&B; also R&B-rooted vocal delivery.
Apple Music editorial identifies melodic dancehall in 3AM (Pull Up).
Pitchfork names trop-house in 3AM; never present this as album-wide dominance.
The critic frames it as radically reimagined contemporary pop.
Experimental electronics and highly synthetic arrangement are pervasive.
NME explicitly calls the songs metamorphic dance-pop.
Explicit album-wide electropop genre tag from music critic editorial.
Contemporary music-critic classification of the album; term is retrospective.
Music critic explicitly tags the record synthpop.
Pitchfork names European dance-pop templates and describes them as part of overall hybrid.
NME highlights experimental, structurally transformative dance-pop throughout.
Pitchfork cites Jeremih-style R&B chords in Out of My Head.
Pitchfork describes 808s and rap-style repetition on I Got It and other sections.
Review identifies PC Music as bubblegum-bass collective; inference to album is indirect.
Clear album-wide pop classification from NME.
Pitchfork identifies synthetic electro-pop production and singles.
Repeated references to corrosive electronics and digital textures.
Club choruses are a repeated pop feature, balanced by ballads.
Pitchfork explicitly calls Gone synth-pop and notes wide use of synths.
Pitchfork describes Swedish Eurodance sound adapted into album production.
NME describes Charli post-Sucker as avant-pop, carried into this album.
EDM drop specifically named for Blame It on Your Love.
Pitchfork classified record Pop/R&B, though this does not mean most tracks are R&B.
Rap-vocal sections with collaborators on Shake It, and hip-hop-related rhythm references.
AOTY metadata associates the release with bubblegum bass; weaker evidence, review before import.
Arena-sized 1980s rock drums feature in reviewer production analysis, not a primarily rock album.
